You can find articles in this magazine on such diverse topics as the death penalty, raising kids, buying a new coat, setting up an internet business, breaking up with a girlfriend, or purchasing the best vodka. There are articles geared toward single men and married men, as well as younger men and middle- aged men.

I like some of the articles found here but there is one problem I have with the writing in Details. It is common to find eye- catching headlines on the cover of Details that tempt you to find out more. This is nothing new and most every magazine does this. But the problem is that many of these eye- popping stories fail to keep you amazed when you read them. Take for example an article in a recent issue. On the front, it reads "Is Your Wife a Bad Mom"? It sound like an engaging, intellectual read. But once you find the article and take in its 1,000+ words, you quickly discover that there is little or no substance. Basically, it simply tells men that accusing your wife of being a bad mom is a risky undertaking that could hurt her feelings. That is it. There is no intellectual analysis or quotes from studies; only the bottom line conclusion that mothers generally don't like to be called incompetent by their husbands. Other headlining articles in this magazine lead to similar disappointment.

The writing in this magazine is on the edge and very blunt. It is common to find several four- letter words in many of the articles and while this doesn't bother me at all, I know that some readers will consider it too raw, too edgy, and too explicit. Details writers have no problem telling it like it is, and this can be both good and bad depending on one's perspective.

Besides the language, some parts of this magazine could offend certain readers; namely the "Anthropology" page at the end. This closing "article" is meant to be humorous, but some readers will not see it that way. I don't know if it has always been this way, but what "Anthropology" does is show a person or multiple people and then asks the question "Gay or ______". For example, I have seen titles like "Gay or Best Friends?", "Gay or Cowboy?", "Gay or Neo Punk Rocker?", and others. With each of these, there is a diagram of sorts with arrows pointing to different clothing and bodily features and short comments about each one. Basically, it is asking you to think about these different attributes of the person or people in the picture and then decide if the way they dress, look, and act makes them gay. I find this silly and immature, but I can see how some readers would find it insulting. I don't know if Details has always done this or if the Anthropology page has been different in the past. But this is how it has been in every issue I have read and it needs to be changed.

Advertisements claim about sixty percent of the pages in each issue of this magazine. They cover products like liquor, cars, electronics, cigarettes, fragrance, etc. Even though this magazine covers lots of different things, the item most often featured in the advertisements is clothing. The magazine seems to have a penchant for high fashion and it devotes more pages to expensive clothing than anything else. And each issue often has its own unique smell, thanks to all of the cologne samples. You can flip through the pages and find several samples in each issue, with many of the latest and trendiest scents from the biggest names in cologne.

Overall, I am torn between liking or not liking Details Magazine. I like some of the articles on food, drink, politics and the like. But I don't necessarily like the shallow fluff that is often substituted for an intellectual discussion and I can understand how some readers would find certain aspects of this magazine insulting. This magazine is deserving of only about two and one- half stars which I will round up to three stars and give a small recommendation. Some will like this magazine and some will not. It's all a matter of what you like to read about and whether or not you can handle a magazine that pushes the envelope.

reviews.title: Sunset Fills You With Visions of the Western U.S.
reviews.text:
Sunset is a magazine dedicated to the people, culture, and lifestyle of the American west. This magazine divides its space among many different topics, such as food and entertainment, travel, recreation, gardening and more.

I have been reading this magazine for about six months now and there are several things about it that make it worthwhile. The thing that stands out the most are the photographs, and I'm not talking about just the stunning scenery one normally associates with the West (like the National Parks or the coastline). Even the ordinary pictures are striking. In the Gardening section, for example, it is common to find pictures of family homes that have beautifully landscaped yards full of blossoming flowers and colorful plants. In the Home & Design section, one can find nice photographs of home interiors, showing different designs and furniture.

One of the most unique qualities of Sunset is the fact that it is published in five different editions. There is a specially designed issue for the Northwest (Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Alaska, and British Columbia), Northern California (Northern California and the majority of Nevada), Southern California (Southern California and Hawaii), The Southwest (Arizona, New Mexico, and the Las Vegas area of Nevada), and Rocky Mountain (Montana, Wyoming, Colorado, and Utah). This is a nice idea and it's one that other magazines should consider emulating. Based on where you live or where you have an active interest, this will be the region that your issue spends its pages covering. My subscription is for the Northern California region, so I am treated each month to articles about places like San Francisco, Sacramento, Reno (Nevada), Lake Tahoe, etc.

One of the specialties of this magazine is food and it is common to find recipes throughout every issue. There is a special section set aside for food, but one can expect to find food articles and recipes everywhere as they read. Even the cover page of each issue features a food dish. And as you might guess, the featured recipes are generally those types of cuisine normally associated with each specific region of the west, with plenty of generic recipes thrown in to make sure everyone has something to cook.

One of the specialty sections of this magazine that I like is the "Value Vacation"- a subsection of Travel & Recreation. This section highlights a specific place to travel and then offers a day by day breakdown of things to do and places to see, with the cost for each itemized so you know exactly what to expect. The highlighted city or tourist area can be anyplace in the west and isn't limited to the region that your issue covers. This section is nice because it lets you see in black & white what it will cost for a few days of budget entertainment. It reminds me of some of the television programs shown on the Travel Channel.

Advertisements cover about 40 to 50 percent of the pages of each issue and they are often found in bunches in the front and back and on alternating pages for much of the rest of each issue (typical for most magazines). The ads can center on all sorts of different things. Because this is a combination travel/culture/food/entertainment/home & garden/living magazine, the ads cover a wide range of products and services, from laundry detergent to credit cards to cat food.

Overall, Sunset has proven itself an enjoyable magazine. I don't live in the western United States but this region is my favorite part of the country, so it makes sense that I would find something of value in this publication. I like the photography, the personal stories, the gardening and decorating ideas, and most other aspects of this magazine. If you're dead set in your ways and refuse to read about anything that deviates from your Eastern, Southern, or Midwestern lifestyle, then you may not like Sunset. But for the majority of people, Sunset has much to offer with pages and pages of eye- catching pictures and friendly articles about life in the American West.

reviews.title: Wine Reviews, News, and More
reviews.text:
Wine Spectator is a good wine magazine that seeks to keep the reader informed about new wine products, wine facts and education, and wine events. This magazine is published 17 times per year, so it is available often enough that most wine lovers will have more than their fill of reading material.

Most of the material in Wine Spectator deals with buying wine, and you can expect to find several rating lists in every issue. The editors of the magazine supply the majority of the wine ratings, so when you read that one wine earned 95 points and another only 80, you need to keep in mind that these ratings are from the perspective of people who have sampled hundreds or even thousands of different wines. And with each rating or analysis, there is often contact information, such as the name of the winery or web page, so that you can learn more and/or inquire on making a purchase.

To help shoppers find the wines in each issue, Wine Spectator includes a detachable card that includes the names of the different featured wines. This is a handy addition, because it eliminates the need to copy down names of wine on paper or attempt to memorize the titles. All you do is check off the wines you like on the card and take it with you to your favorite beverage store for easy reference.

Wine Spectator seems to have an obsession with lists and with outlandish proclamations. It is common to find lists like "World's 100 Greatest Pinot" or "The 50 Finest California Reds". Consumers are attracted to listings, and that is probably why the magazine gave in and made lists a regular part of most issues. And it is common to find extreme statements like "This is the best Cabernet Sauvignon on the Planet" or "Greatest German White Wine Ever". The publication does this to attract attention and sell more issues, but it could get annoying to some readers.

In spite of these few annoyances, Wine Spectator is still a good magazine. The writers at Wine Spectator are very good, very convincing, and very persuasive. They really know wine, and it comes through in their articles and recommendations. The editors articulate themselves very well and they know just the right way to describe the different brands and styles. It all adds up to a very informative magazine publication on the world of wine.

reviews.title: Bridal Guide Helps Make Your Wedding Day Complete
reviews.text:
Bridal Guide is a lengthy magazine designed to appeal to brides in waiting and to those women who see marriage on the horizon. This magazine is devoted to bridal fashion and to other things that are involved in making the day special and memorable. Besides the fashion, one can read about wedding planning, honeymoon ideas, photography, and other wedding- related things.

When you read a copy of Bridal Guide, what stands out more than anything are the photos. This is the main reason people read this magazine in the first place: To look at wedding attire and compare different styles. Models wearing wedding gowns are abundant in this publication and some of the bridal gowns they adorn are quite stunning. To help future brides make a possible purchase, it is common to find a phone number and/or a web site with the majority of the photos. Bridal attire is the main focus of this magazine, but there are also some pictures of grooms and of other wedding party members, with models displaying other fashions for sale, once again complete with phone number and web page.

The part of this magazine that focuses its attention on honeymoons and travel is probably my favorite part of the issue. What I like is the fact that this is one part of the magazine that can appeal/apply to anyone, regardless of marital status. These honeymoon tips and destination information provide some good reading material for the bride to be or anyone else who happens to read the magazine.

Bridal Guide is a very lengthy publication, with each issue containing around 500 pages! This is more than double the length of most other magazines and it can make the issue seem a little overwhelming at times. Also, this magazine is saturated with ads. Since the majority of the gown- clad models are, in effect, advertisements for a specific fashion brand, one can expect to find ads covering the vast majority of this magazine's pages. This could be annoying to some, but one must bear in mind that the magazine's focus is wedding planning, so excessive advertising is expected.

For young brides- to- be or bridal wannabes, this is a handy magazine to have around. It's very long, but it contains lots of fashion and wedding planning ideas to make the big day one to remember forever.

reviews.title: The Many Challenges of Business Ownership
reviews.text:
Entrepreneur magazine is one of my favorite business publications and it's the type of magazine I can count on for up- to- date information on business startups and for possible resolutions of common problems to the small business owner. A monthly publication, this magazine is designed to appeal to those who are presently owners of a small enterprise or who aspire to open their own business in the near future.

What I enjoy most about this magazine are its personal articles- stories about ordinary people like you and me who have successfully started a new business venture. These people share their success stories with the reader, offering insight on what strategies helped them reach their present level of success and what challenges they still face. The people featured in the articles are more down to earth types who own smaller companies, making the magazine more realistic and something I and others can better relate to. Many other business magazines spend too much time interviewing billionaire CEO's and others who, while they may have some interesting stories to share, live lifestyles and have problems that only someone of their stature can relate.

On the practical side, Entrepreneur contains many timely articles about common issues/problems/challenges that arise when you own your own company. Money, marketing, management, and other key topics are covered in each issue, with a regular department for these critical aspects of business ownership. In these sections, you can learn about tax law changes, legal issues with benefits, and other related topics.

Entrepreneur organizes each issue quite nicely, with colored tabs on the pages that indicate which section (money, technology, marketing, etc.) they pertain to. This makes it that much easier to sift through, to find the information you need. And there is a section titled "Sources" that helps to index the different services and companies mentioned in each issue.

Overall, this is a useful, practical magazine that can come in very handy for present business owners and for those who have an interest in proprietorship. It keeps business owners up to date with the latest changes in laws and it offers some creative solutions to the everyday problems that small businesses encounter each day.

reviews.title: Living in and Learning About America's Island State
reviews.text:
Hawaii Magazine is a very good publication for those who have an interest in America's fiftieth state. This magazine brings the world of the Hawaiian Islands to your home every month, with facts, figures, and photos taken from this island chain paradise.

One thing about Hawaii Magazine that is different from what you might expect is that it covers more than just travel. When I read this publication for the first time, I was surprised at the contents within. I always assumed this was a magazine solely about travel and tourism. While travel, resorts, and related topics are an important part of this magazine, they are not the only part. The rest of Hawaii Magazine deals with cultural and native topics. It lets you discover the people who inhabit these islands. You get to learn about Hawaiian customs, holidays, art, dress, and culture.

With the emphasis on culture, Hawaii Magazine is a learning experience. The people responsible for the publication of this magazine want readers to come away with a better understanding of what it means to be Hawaiian and to live in this island chain. They want you to think of Hawaii as more than just a nice, warm, sunny place to visit. They want you to learn about the people that inhabit Hawaii: How they dress, how they celebrate events, how they interact with others, etc.

If I had to name a few cons to this magazine, they would have to be the publications short length (less than 100 pages per issue) and its infrequent publication (every two months). Other than these negative aspects, most everything else about this magazine makes it worthwhile to read. It's an educational lesson on the people and the lifestyle of those we call Hawaiian.

reviews.title: Living and Thriving in a House Made With Logs
reviews.text:
Log Home Living is a good magazine for those who have an active interest in buying and living in a home made from logs. This publication covers everything you need to know about this type of living, from the planning of a home all the way through the financing, the furnishing, and the maintenance.

What I enjoy most about this magazine is the fine photographs found on most every page. I don't really have much interest in living in this type of home, but the photos are very appealing and enticing. Some of them are taken inside of log homes, letting you see firsthand the dividends that some attention to design can bring. Some of them are taken on the exterior, allowing readers to see the country landscape and marvel in the natural beauty.

Another nice feature of this magazine is the abundance of phone numbers and web sites for goods and services. If you find something you like, you will know exactly where to turn for more information. If you find a product or service you like that doesn't list a source, don't worry- there are some special index sections in the back with lists of products from the current issue, referenced by page number, showing the company name, phone, and web site so you can find what you like and make a purchase.

On the negative side, a magazine like this one contains LOTS of advertisements. The majority of them are found at the end of the magazine, but there are plenty of them throughout and you cannot turn more than a few pages before finding one. I would estimate that more than two- thirds of the pages have some sort of advertisement.

Since a good deal of this magazine is dedicated to furnishing, interior design, landscaping, and maintenance, there is something here to suit every home owner's needs. Even if you don't have an interest in log homes, you can still find plenty to enjoy in Log Home Living. The pictures alone make it worth a look.

reviews.title: Attention Female Shoppers
reviews.text:
This magazine is a product of CondeNet publishing and it is aimed at the younger female market, roughly from ages 18 to 30. This publication is a shopper's paradise, with more advertising than most any other magazine on the market.

I got a complimentary subscription to this magazine one day and I accepted, not only because it was free, but also because I really didn't know it was a woman's fashion magazine. With a title like "Lucky", there were all sorts of possibilities. It could have been about gambling, sweepstakes, or about getting lucky. I didn't know it was a woman's magazine, so I accepted it. And from what I can see, this magazine is one of average worth to the average person and it will appeal mostly to younger women.

Fashion covers a good amount of the magazine's 200 plus pages. Beauty tips are another important area of coverage. It is also common to see samples of different products inside the pages of each issue. Things like perfume samples, shampoo, and other things can be found buried somewhere within each copy. The coverage includes casual as well as high- class clothing and beauty products, with most of it falling at the upper end of the cost scale.

If you can tolerate the clogging of advertisements, this magazine might be a good choice for the younger female crowd that likes to keep in- tune with the latest styles and trends. Outside of that targeted market, however, I don't see much use for Lucky magazine. The photography is very good and the presentation is professional, but the magazine will likely be rated average by a large cross- section of the population.

reviews.title: Good Eats, Fine Drinks, and Having Fun
reviews.text:
Food and Wine is a pretty good magazine for those who enjoy the finer things in life when it comes to unusual cuisine and expensive fermented beverages. This publication is usually very long- over 250 pages- and its packed full of recipes, travel excursions to wine growing regions, and general facts about different varieties of wine and where to find them.

One thing about this magazine that surprised me at first is the emphasis on the food. I know the magazine is titled "Food and Wine", but my initial impression was that this would be a magazine devoted entirely to wine with occasional mention of the foods that go with wine. It isn't like that at all. The food sections and the recipes are just as important as the featured wines. Recipes are so frequent, in fact, that the magazine even has an index located near the front with all the recipes listed by food type, showing the page number to turn to for the recipe.

Besides the frequent talk about food and wine, this magazine is also dedicated to entertaining. I have heard it suggested that this magazine should change its name to "Food, Wine, and Entertainment". It would make sense, because conviviality and high- class partying are certainly an important component of this magazine.

There is one thing about Food and Wine that I wish was different. I appreciate the factual information and I like the personal touch that you find in some of the stories about winery owners, chefs, and the like. But I think Food and Wine gets a little too sidetracked from time to time in its reporting. For example, it is common to find stories that talk about subjects like home decorating. This would be fine in a magazine about home design, but I don't think it belongs in a magazine like this.

Overall, this is still a good publication. Lovers of great eats and fine drinks will enjoy it the most. It's worth taking a look, if nothing else, just for the recipes. Even if you're not a frequent imbiber of the fruit of the vine, there is still something of interest to be found in the pages of this magazine.

reviews.title: Technology and Public Policy
reviews.text:
Technology magazines are often a little bit on the boring side due to their limited appeal that makes them readable only to those who work in or have an avid interest in this field. IEEE Spectrum, however, is a little bit different. It has plenty of information on the latest advancements in technology, like other tech publications, but from a different "spectrum", if you will.

What sets this magazine apart from the rest is the personal and political topics that make their way into each issue. You can read about topics like global warming, tariffs, technology regulations, and general business ethics. These different topics are blended together with the magazine's core subject of technology and the result is a publication that is more readable than most in the tech field.

Another nice thing about Spectrum is the minimal amount of advertising. What few ads you will see are entirely related in some way to technology. You won't see an ad for a car, boat, home financing, or other product or service like you do in most every other magazine in America. This magazine sticks with technology for its ads and because of this, the few ads that exist seem even less common than they already are.

This magazine is a little shorter than other monthly publications, with each issue containing about 50 to 80 pages. This is the length I expect in a weekly magazine- not a monthly one. The publishers need to improve and expand the number of pages. A magazine this short doesn't provide enough reading material for an entire month.

Still, IEEE Spectrum is a good technology magazine. The combination of political, economic, and social topics keeps this publication from getting too dry and too technical. It makes it much easier to read than other magazines of the same genre.

reviews.title: Golf's Best Magazine Publication
reviews.text:
Golfers share many things in common and one of these is an often fanatical love for the game. For these types, nothing can take the place of heading to the nearest golf course, but Golf Digest comes very close. This magazine contains over 200 pages each month, dedicated exclusively to the sport of golf.

The things that set Golf Digest apart from the competition are the numerous articles about learning and improving your game and the personal stories and interviews. Other golfing publications attempt to help you learn, but they often get too mechanical. Golf Digest shows you how to improve your game with tips from professionals, including some of the star- studded members of the golfing elite like Tiger Woods.

Besides all the tips and tricks, Golf Digest also shows the personal side of the sport with interviews and more intimate stories about the many colorful personalities in the game. This personal dimension adds greatly to the magazine's overall appeal, providing great reading material to complement the more instructional side of the magazine.

Golfing Digest may not be as great as a day spent on your favorite golf course, but it comes close. I consider it the best publication of its kind and I recommend it to anyone with an interest in the game.

reviews.title: We were Sailing Along
reviews.text:
Are you the type who enjoys a nice excursion in a sailboat? If so, then you will probably enjoy Sail magazine. This publication is one of dozens available on the newsstands that cover the sport and hobby of sailing, but I feel its one of the best around.

What makes me feel so strongly about this magazine is the fact that the articles and advice are written by actual sailors. This magazine doesn't waste the reader's time with articles composed by so- called professional writers. Instead, it sticks with the people who know sailing better than anyone: the sailors themselves. This makes the magazine more believable and more respectable.

Sail divides its time between factual articles and ones that are more personable in nature. The factual articles cover things like how to maneuver a boat in different directions; what to look for when you shop for a new navigation device; the advantages and disadvantages of catamarans; etc. These factual stories are intended more for those who own boats and want to keep them in tip- top condition. The other articles deal with personal stories, and they rank among my favorites in each issue. These articles feature individuals and families who share their sea- going experiences with you.

Sail also has lots of reviews of boat- related products and plenty of ads in the back of each issue for shoppers who are looking for a boat. Ads in the rest of the magazine are scattered around, but they tend to stick mostly to boating and related products. The reviews are nice, but I would prefer to see more opinions from more people, to make comparisons.

Sail magazine has many great qualities, and they add up to a well- rounded publication- a magazine that I feel is the best in its field. Whether you sail for sport or for leisure, Sail magazine is probably the best of its kind. Great photography, informative articles, and personal stories place this magazine in a league of its own.

reviews.title: A great career while it lasted
reviews.text: Finally settled in last night to watch this movie. Let me start by saying that I love a good mystery and that I usually enjoy these kind of movies. Not much more can I say that hasn't been said before. First, the acting was absolutely awful. The movie is so scripted, it's almost as if the actors are reading their lines. The roles and characters are more than predictable (i.e. you have all token nationalities in the 'bad guy' gang, so they are equal opportunity offenders). I found most of the action in the fight scenes to be totally absurd. I could no more see Kim B. slinging a tire iron at someone (and getting it lodged in the victim's nostrils) then my mother doing it. It was almost comical. The underlying piece of Kim's marriage to an abusive man, was also ridiculously scripted and acted (damn, if any housewife kept a house as dirty and junk filled as she did, who wouldn't be yelling at her from time to time?). Anyway, just reliving this movie to write this review is painful. The movie was like a bad Saturday Night Live/MadTV skit. Run, don't walk, from buying or even renting this one.

reviews.title: Not exactly like the book, but good just the same
reviews.text: I bought the DVD of Angela's Ashes after purchasing the audio CD of the book (which I highly, highly recommend). Starting with the audion CD, I was enthralled in listening to Frank McCourt's own voice (almost as if he was telling his whole childhood story just to me). I actually was so disappointed when the book ended (because it had me so captivated), I couldn't wait to see the movie. So, I bought it. Now, the strengths of the movie are that you get to see some beautifulm and tragic, areas of  where the McCourts came from. The acting was pretty good. The bad part for me was that it seemed so depressing. It was raining constantly (which I know it does frequently in Ireland, but not every day and all the time. Even the audio CD talked of days with sunshine. I think the creator/director of the movie was trying awfully hard to make the McCourt's childhood similar to people living in some kind of an abusive/prison type setting. The audio CD had me laughing out loud at some of the most tragic parts of his life, as Frank inserted his phenominal sense of humor into everything. I didn't seem to get that same feel from the movie. Many scenes that were discussed in the book were either left out or glossed over in the movie all together. After hearing the CD, I felt enlightened, enchanted, craving to hear more of his life (so, I bought 'TIS last week). The movie just wanted to make me cry and get on my knees to thank God I wasn't raised in that area of Ireland during the 1940's. I recommend it only if you have read/are going to read the real book behind this. It is worth seeing to be able to relate to the town and scenery that you will hear/read about in the book.

reviews.title: Here we go again
reviews.text:
So for all of those who think by buying the current season you will get to see all episodes before they even air, learn how this works. You will get the next episode AFTER it airs on the Hallmark channel. Now if only Hallmark would release it to Amazon in a timely manner, the show should be waiting for you the next morning. But Hallmark shows rarely show up the way other networks do.

As far as the show, it has been terrible this season! This is no longer a feel good show that most of us go to Hallmark for. They have over done it on all the negativity with a few of the female characters this season. It’s one thing to show the couple’s having an issue here and there but the whole season has been about Clara being angry with Jesse and with Faith making sure Carson knows how much he keeps messing up. Elizabeth's character is the most unlikeable person at this point. She is rude, bitter and all around totally unpleasant. The love triangle gets really old and they’ve over done it with this one on this show. Who cares at this point who Elizabeth picks and who cares what happens to her character?

reviews.title: Decent Sound Quality

The sound quality is good and more than adequate for use with the computer. My husband primarily uses the speakers for gaming and watching videos. For an audiophile, it may not be suffice. The sound is pretty clear. They do take up a lot of space compared to more compact computer speakers. Overall, my husband is pleased with them.

reviews.text: My daughter plays the cello in her high school orchestra. The students share rosin, so my daughter was pleased to have her own. As a former viola player, it seems to be a fine quality product.  It's raised so the edges don't interfere with application. It's definitely low dust. The shape of the container is easy to grip and allows easy application to the bow. The lid completely covers the rosin and offers adequate protection from breaking. She did have to scratch it up a little before using it.

reviews.title: Decent Starter Instrument
reviews.text: Let me start with saying that my teenage daughter likes this petite guitar. She's been wanting a guitar for years, but we haven't gotten around to getting her one. She plays the cello and owns a Ukulele. This is larger than a Ukulele. It can be tuned, but it gets out of tune very quickly. If she sets it down for a while and goes back to it, it always needs to be retuned. The actual guitar is cheaply made. There are some rough edges and chips. She did get a small splinter from playing it. She has been playing around on it almost daily. She does get a little frustrated with the constant tuning, but even with those issues, she still likes it. We're probably going to buy her a full sized, higher quality guitar for her birthday this spring since she's shown us that she is serious about having one.

reviews.title: User Friendly Keyboard
reviews.text: I purchased a cheap, no name brand keyboard for my teenager a year ago. It was not a good quality keyboard at all. She disliked it so much, she rarely played it. I got her a nice Yamaha one which was much better. It was also a higher price. My son wanted to play around with a keyboard to create MIDI sounds for his video games and my teens weren't thrilled about sharing a keyboard, so I got him this Casio instrument.  I would say that this Casio one is a nice middle ground keyboard. It's better than the cheap no name one It's completely adequate for a beginning teenager (or child) who wants to learn or play around with a keyboard. He did have to purchase a specialized cable to hook it up to his laptop, but that was expected. The keys sound a little plastic sounding, but not as bad as the first keyboard I got. The plastic sounds are pretty standard for portable keyboards in my opinion.  This keyboard has been fairly user friendly. It was easy to set up. For the price, it does a good job. When my son played with the cheap one, he expressed his desire for a better keyboard. With this one, he's satisfied with it's performance for his needs.

reviews.title: Great for Beginners & Non-Professional Musicians!
reviews.text: About a year ago, I bought my teenage daughter a cheaper, no name keyboard. It was in the $80 range. She plays the cello, ukulele, and guitar and wanted to learn how to play the keyboard. She had a lot of complaints with the keyboard and lost interest in it after a short while. I thought maybe she would have more success with a brand name keyboard instead. And so far, so good. The sound is so much better. The keys don't sound as plastic as the other keyboard. They still don't sound like a real piano, but it's definitely much better than the cheap one. This one has more features, sounds/voices, and more than the other keyboard. The power adapter doesn't come with it, but the old one didn't come with one either. The specs for the adapter are on the description page, so my husband was able to find one at home that works. This keyboard is perfect for beginners or hobbyist players. It would probably not suffice for professional musicians, but it has been quite good enough for my teenager and has gotten her interested again in learning how to play.

My daughter plays the cello and ukulele, so she does have some experience with stringed instruments. She used an app on her phone and was able to tune it. She did find it a more difficult to tune than her other instruments. As with other new strings, they do go out of tune rather quickly until they have had adequate time to stretch. The quality of the guitar set is pretty decent. It is a good starter set. My daughter loves it!

reviews.text:
My daughter plays the cello. She uses school owned instruments. Rosin is provided, but it is shared among the students. She has been wanting her own rosin for class and for the summer months when she will take her instrument home for the summer. The shape of this rosin is cute. At first I wasn't sure about the shape, but it works. I used to play the viola when I was a child and my rosin was rectangle shaped. Mine also had firm sides, so when the rosin got used and shrunk in size, it was difficult to use. This one has open sides so that won't be an issue. The shape is easy to hold on to, too. It doesn't produce much dust.

*I purchased this at a discounted price in exchange for my honest & unbiased review. My thoughts & opinions are my own.

reviews.title: Multiple Uses
reviews.text:
My daughter plays the cello, but the designated practice room in our home does not have overhead lighting. The lights provided by the lamps in that room just don't provide adequate lighting for her. She can practice easily during daylight hours, but once the sun goes down, she can't see well at all. So the Veluxio music stand light has been a blessing! It clips on to her music stand (or other pieces of furniture if needed) and with the flexible arms she can adjust the lights perfectly on her music. I really like that it comes with a power cord, USB cord & batteries. The plastic clip is easy to open. The LED lights are nice & bright. In addition to using for music, it makes a great book light, too!

*I was provided with the music stand light for the purpose of trying out & reviewing. My thoughts & opinions are my own.

reviews.title: Great keyboard pantyhose
reviews.text: Fits my Korg Triton Extreme 88 keyboard nicely.  No sag with just a little stretch that is fits smooth across the top and snug along the bottom edges and corners.  No problem leaving cables plugged in with the cover on.  Easy on, easy off.

reviews.title: Built like a Brick - Which is Good
reviews.text: This is a solidly-built straight CW keyer.  I've "book-learned" morse code, but keying morse is another thing.  I practice using this with a morse code app that reads and decodes sound signals.  Then I can tell whether I'm keying the letters and numbers correctly, and whether I'm pausing between letters and words correctly at different speeds.  It works fine with either a 9V battery or a 12V DC adapter.  The sound module is definitely analog, with some variation in pitch ("chirp"), but it's not a problem for practice.  If connected to a radio, you must disconnect the key from the sound module hence it will not be used at all, so the chirp from the sound generation module isn't an issue.  The tension and throw adjustments are a tried-and-true design that work well for light touch activation and release.

reviews.title: Pretty & I love it!
reviews.text: Lovely ink. Writes well. The right amount of wet/dry. Currently using it in both a platinum curidas (f) & a pelican twist (m) & it writes well in both.  Beautiful color & flows nicely. It has not clogged up my nibs.

reviews.title: 2 excellent 1 extremely dry (blue)
reviews.text: Overall I’m pretty happy with this purchase bc the ink is good & I’ve purchased it before.  The green is gorgeous.  The purple didn’t really wow me, but it flows nicely. The blue however is a disappointment bc it’s extremely dry & keeps drying in my pen. I am using the inks in the same type of pen- platinum curidas & all have same size nib. So the only difference is the actual ink.  I’m gonna try to mix a little of the ink with a tiny bit of glycerin next time I refill it & see if that helps it to stay wetter & not dry out in my pen. Aside from that I love their ink. Think I just received a dud this time with the blue.

reviews.title: I don’t get the reviews. Mine are garbage.
reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:63276c19932aa4f3687042b8b9f8613c]] Update: tried again to return them. I have prime. Amazon wants $7.99 to pick them up. Why? Bc I return garbage products & I don’t feel like I should be penalized when third party sellers & amazon send damaged/defective products & then expect me to be happy with them & keep them. Why should I bear the burden of a billion dollar plus corporation as a disabled veteran living on disability? These skip all over the place. The yellow won’t write no matter how much I shake the ball bearing. It and the black give a second of ink & stop. I even tried warming the ink up. The black finally became more viscous, but the yellow won’t lay down. If you have a fast hand & are used to taking fast notes these are useless. At least my set is. Garbage. Utter & complete garbage. Some work better if you write slow like a toddler, but I have never had to slow my hand with a zebra fountain pen nor any of the 200 others I own. And you don’t have to shake the zebra pen!

I purchased these bc of the reviews. Maybe I receive a bad batch. Idk. Mine are awful. I have fountain pens I purchased online for a dollar and less that works better & that write every single time I pick them up. Half of these did not even work after I attached the ink. I had to squeeze the cartridge repeatedly & even then I’m lucky if I get anything to come out. For $18 I was expecting to at least get something that would write every time I picked it up. These are a scratchy mess. I have tried them on cheap paper & expensive Tomoe River paper with the same results. I have hundreds of fountain pens, but I was looking for something that I could visually see at a moment’s glance what color was in the pen & I thought these would work. I will give them a few more days, but if the ink doesn’t settle in & lubricate the innards so that the writing experience is improved then I will definitely be sending these back bc they are garbage as-is.

reviews.title: Ordering Ink online: never a good idea I guess.
reviews.text: It’s a beautiful color, but even though it had been packed extremely well imo it still arrived & showed considerable loss of ink due to shipping/handling disturbances.  It also left a stain on my bathroom vanity that I am still working on & thankfully it’s just a small one as I placed paper towels down before I opened the mess.  Next time I receive a bottle like this I’m just going to rinse it off, pat it dry, & slip a non-latex glove over it to keep everything in the vicinity safe including my hands bc the ink stained the label & wont come off except if my hands happen to be wet/moist.  The ink works well on both Tomoe River paper & cheap notebook paper & dries quickly.  As for the ink itself: I love it!  I don’t understand why it stained my vanity tho bc to my knowledge it’s not supposed to be waterproof.  Luckily after much scrubbing there is only a tiny mark left & I know it’s there, but I am really hoping my LL does not notice it.  Gonna try a little bleach on it next.  Also, I was able to mix a bit of it with a J Herbin red ink (scented red rose I believe) that I had on hand to get another shade of purple & I am quite pleased with it.  It is currently in a Dryden pen rn & it’s working beautifully with zero issues. This ink R&K is in a Lamy  “Candy” purple pen & is also working beautifully.  I wish they offered the inks in glass bottles instead of the cheap plastic.  Tho I recently received a bottle of Pilot Iroshiziku ink with a cracked lid & zero ink as it had obviously been upside down at some point during transit so glass is no guarantee that ink doesn’t get damaged. I’m disabled so I generally order everything online as it’s easier for me, but it appears I am going to have to venture out of my cave at some point. Lol. The ink is lovely if you can get one that has not been damaged or lost too much of it’s contents en route as I have.  I did notice that the cap on mine was dented & I believe that’s probably what allowed the ink to escape as they always tell us not to buy dented cans at grocery stores!  Things are only as good as their weakest links.

reviews.title: Mine are iffy at best.
reviews.text: Idk if I just got a bad batch which is possible I suppose bc let’s face it sometimes companies have bad manufacturing runs, but all 4 of my pens are a total pain to use. They skip or the ink just does not flow at all no matter how hard I press on the Nov & then I get a puddle of ink.  Every once in a blue moon if I dip them in ink they seem to work a bit better, but it’s definitely not how they were meant to be used. I am not a newbie either. I own well over 200 fountain pens & calligraphy pens of versing widths & I have a large collection of inks as well. I also tried these out on every type of paper I have from Tomoe River to Mead & composition notebooks, but the pens I have are just useless for me as they will not write fluidly.  If I wanted to stop & start a hundred x I would just stick with my dip pens.  These are a huge let down as they have so many high reviews & I just wasn’t expecting them to be so awful.  Idk if I’m going to try the amazon replacement or not.  In my experience I tend to get another item from the same bad quality lot (or worse).  Decisions, decisions.

reviews.title: Quality not as pictured in advertising.
reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:ffd2a834f42a38fd089e2bfa848e4b5d]] Idk what to say bc what I received looks nothing like the one advertised. What I received looks like someone poured motor oil on leather after they stamped it then went on a long lunch & came back & tried to fix the mess they left on the leather. It looks like they tried to distress or something which I hate to begin with as I’m not a fan of fake distressing. I find that seems to be the norm when the leather is not the best quality. When the leather is thinner or more scratched up as this is the sellers seem to think it’s best to distress it.

The stamping itself is well done. The only problem with it is that the leather is so thin & thinner even in some places that it has created humps in the cover front & back. I am not joking about the motor oil. It feels & smells like motor oil. Their is a slick substance on my hands after touching it & I am allergic to petroleum products so I’ve had to wash my hands several times & put on gloves. The distressing job was so uneven that if I decide to keep the journal I will definitely not keep it in this incarnation. I will definitely use leather cleaner to remove whatever I can sue to my allergies & then I will have to cover it with something else that I’m not allergic to, but that just adds time & money to this so idk what I’m going to do yet. I’ve even thought of painting it & sealing it. Fortunately the dye job on the front isn’t as bad as the one on the back & I’m the only one that will see it as it’s not a gift for anyone except myself.

I like the locking mechanism & feel they did a good job on thst tho it was covered in the oil too. That has made it easy to open tho. Lol. However, bc of the locking mechanism this is not a journal you will be able to paste or collage many things into. It’s a straight up writing journal imo bc it’s in no way expandable due to the locking device. Tho I suppose if your crafty/handy you can change out the rivets in the back & add a longer piece of leather there after you have filled it to ur heart’s desire.

As for the paper I don’t find it any better than any paper I’ve had in similar journals. It has flecks & bits of other papers which I personally don’t care for bc I use fountain pens & dip pens & my pens will skip on the uneven surfaces & that is literally on every page. There are also quite a few wrinkled pages in the journal which you can find with homemade journals.

So at this point I just don’t know. I need to think about it a bit more. If I had received a journal that looked as good as the advertised one & was not covered in oil & I would definitely keep it & just use different pens or use it for watercolor or bird sketches. This one requires more thought. I definitely would not give this as a gift to anyone unless I ordered it to be delivered to me & had a chance to clean it up & check it out first, but if you are a crafty person who likes a challenge or is willing to take a chance & hope for one like the pic then idk maybe take a chance?

reviews.title: Packing is awful will update pen review later
reviews.text: Literally one of the worst packing jobs I’ve seen.  It’s the lightest pen I have ever used & as I am post surgery on my dominant hand & am used to less than 5 minutes of writing even remotely comfortably I absolutely love that part.  I think it’s pricey for what it is though. The Pilot Petit are $3 on Jet pens. 8 x cheaper & imho write just as well. Where this has the advantage for me is tho I am a woman I am tall & have man hands so said two hubbies. Bloody mean things to say if you ask me. Lol.  I am in love with it even though I hate the price point & truly believe it to be massively overpriced for plastic, but being s fountain pen junkie with well over a hundred including Montblanc I fully intend to buy bc thst is what we fountain pen ppl do. We collect them in all shapes & sizes. I have 5 kids & I tend to collect them in both my & my children’s & my grandchildren’s favorite colors.  Some I gift while I am alive & others they will only inherit bc I use them daily for writing & art.  It is a little beauty & I love that the cap screws on.  This mint color is beautiful & just happens to match a cutting mat I picked up at Wally World recently. Lol. Yay me!

reviews.title: Defective hardware & workmanship
reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:c4ffdd909a55f78e5a83951e34c4528e]] Unfortunately I received a pen that has some very bad metal parts that has the actual gold finish missing in quite a few places & is scratched up in many others.  That means the metal parts actually test my skin & cut it because the metal is actual quite jagged in many places. I don’t know if the metal pieces were dropped or were caught in some machinery or what, but it makes for a very unpleasant feeling when you hold it & a very unsafe result when it cut my fingers in several places.  I liked the look of the ribbed design of the metal on the pen, but it made for a less than ideal experience when actually holding the pen as it was uncomfortable.  It’s a very pretty pen & I found it quite beautiful even though it honestly triggered issues with my vertigo. Something about the design where it looks almost holographic & like the design is actually moving kicked my vertigo into high gear which is unfortunate bc the design was the entire reason I purchased the pen in the first place. Lol.  The issue with the workmanship should be able to ne seen in the pics as there are quite a few globs of resin or acrylic down the side of the pen which are a darker yellow stain than the rest of the pen & there are globs of what must be wood pulp or shavings in the resin that end up sitting directly on top of the top layer & you can both see them & feel them when you run your hand over the pen. Which is extremely annoying to someone who likes to pet her fountain pens.  It would definitely be worth checking back in a couple of months as the crafter gets better at their trade and/or uses better materials.  However, right now with these damaged metal materials with nicks, scratches, & paint missing & with the flaws/damages to the wood I’m not in the mood for a replacement & I intend to go for a return/refund.  Though I do hope to try this seller again at a later date if I see an improvement in the issues bc I prefer hand made fountain pens.

reviews.title: My pen is utter garbage & leaks like a sieve.
reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:b5de3fbb67572893aa86f7052023b9ba]] I’m dumbfounded by the great reviews. Maybe I just received a dud? Idk.  My pen leaks like a sieve as you can see in the pics & by the ink collected on my fingers. The cap will not post which makes me crazy.  The clip is askew. It’s like a third grader put it together with left over fittings & tried to make it fit. The fittings are a hot mess too. The gold is all scratched, dinged, & dented & it came like that right out of the packaging.  I also can’t u deer and why they have 2 shades of teal making up the pen body. The very tip is one shader & it just looks like they ran out of resin imo.  The resin itself has some obvious impurities in it. Idk if it was dusty where these were made or what, but something definitely got into the mix that produced this pen.  I am a fountain pen freak & I have purchased pens off eBay for 99 cents or less that write 100x better than this pen. The nib is so scratchy it has actually torn paper & I have a very light hand & use pricey papers.  I love Jane Davenport stuff, but after seeing the cancer warnings no thx.  I’ll purchase from artists who care as much about my health as I do.

reviews.title: Damaged! Stamps don’t pick up the ink properly.
reviews.text: I’ve used Carter’s for 4 decades in a work environment & home environment for arts & crafts, but I have never in my life received one looking like this. Looks like some kid stick their fingers in it.  Lol. And the seal actually looked as tho it had been previously compromised when I went to open it. I wish I had thought to take a pic of that.  I’m less than thrilled bc I needed this asap for a current project.  The front of the pad is pretty beat up too.  It has a very obvious dent in it which I would assume is when the interior pad got messed up making it hard to get stamps to pick up the ink evenly without applying a lot of pressure & then you get parts of the stamp that aren’t part of the design. This seems like a scratch & dent sale ink pad to me which sucks bc I love Carter’s & have used them for decades as I stated before.  The pad appears to be inked well & is not dry. It even seems to close pretty well considering the huge dent in the lid, but it does not work for the purposes I purchased it for. I’m hoping I can return it or exchange it.

reviews.title: Excellent! Buy it. Buy lots in fact!
reviews.text: New to this brand & as a huge fan & collector of fountain pens I am now a huge fan of this brand.  I purchased the 5-1/2” x 8” size & a smaller one to throw in my purse.  I plan on purchasing more in the future as my fountain pens have finally found a home for their ink & words.  I am very excited about the two ribbons too.  The only issue I see that already annoys me immensely as these are brand spanking new right out of the plastic is that they are missing the green color in several places. Idk if it has flaked off or what, but these were sealed in plastic when I I received them. I have handled them exactly  one time since opening them so idk how that paint job on the cover is going to hold up to daily use.  I knocked of a star for that bc imo they should not be flaking off their color after one handling of extremely light use.  I’m disabled with a bad arm so I’m not able to be rough with it even if I wanted to. Lol. It’s lost the green color at the top & the bottom already.  That is concerning to me as it’s not even been placed on a book shelf yet, but just been lying on a table tray by itself.

reviews.title: Could have been wonderful.  Has execution flaws.
reviews.text:
Update: received replacement & the second is just like the first unfortunately. So I will assume this was made by the same crafter & from the same batch as the last. Again, the paper has been pulled too tightly & ripped through the backing. It has also been cut through the first 30% of the pages at one edge. There are paint pen marking all over the journal inside & out. This one has a cut down the front where maybe they had begun to make a scoring cut in the leather & realized it was going to be too short & then just put the design over it. They did a better job of getting a deeper embossing on this one tho. The finish is worse however. This one has a weird finish almost like pumice stones where it looks kind of crackled & porous Idk if it was done on purpose as a design or not. I wish this crafter would learn to not use paint pens to mark up leather bc it ruins the product. If you try to remove the paint pen you ruin the leather. I am double bummed for having given them a second chance.
Old review:
This could have been a beautiful little hotter notebook. Unfortunately it is not. The ppl that made it decided to use metallic paint pens & permanent markers to mark all their sewing lines ruining the aesthetic. There is not a spot on either side without a blemish. I had resolved myself that if only the inside was ugly I could live with that. Lol. Bc there’s a lot of that irl imo, but it turned out that both the inside & outside had imperfections behind what I was prepared to pay for & live with. As a disabled person I can generally live with a lot lol, but I spend my little bit of money on writing tools & I like them to be nice. This could have been a thing of true beauty as it reminds me of several Levenger notebooks I own. Sadly, while the idea was great the execution is lacking. I hope they will do it right next time bc it’s the perfect size to throw into a purse or backpack for a short trip or even a longer jaunt if you bring paper refills. The paper quality was not what I was hoping for either & as it arrived torn & already pulling away from its base I would not have used it anyways. As it is it is a hard no for me in its current state. I hope that either the seller or amazon will do right me. Someone should definitely be doing quality inspection checks bc this would not have passed even a rudimentary one. The metallic silver paint pen was a glaring no staring me right in the face the second I opened it up. The black permanent marker while it did match the journal better was still extremely obvious & still extremely annoying to see. It’s a well thought out design in my estimation just an extremely flawed execution. I hope the seller tweaks their issues & offers it in other colors bc I would totally try again.

reviews.title: Lovely, but front bent  corner & toner (?) splotches throughout.
reviews.text: It’s a nice heavy journal with thick pages.  The rose gold color is very pretty. Of course the first thing I noticed when I pulled it from the package was that the upper right hand corner had already been bent.  For some reason the quick reference page has been glued in weirdly imo so that there is no margin to the left & it makes it hard to write ur information there.  I haven’t written mine in there yet bc my entire book seems to have toner or printer ink or something on every single page like someone decided to just sprinkle some fairy dust on every page.  As I intend to use this partly as an art journal I would prefer one without the added splotches all over.  I believe there are 43 sheets of lined paper after the journal section & I am quite happy about that added bonus.  The envelope in the back is quite roomy & will hold a lot of receipts.  It’s a pretty journal & I suspect I will buy more from the manufacturer in the future albeit hopefully without these issues bc this one needs to be replaced & hopefully Amazon will do so.

reviews.title: Wrong pens!!!
reviews.text: My review is whacked bc I received the wrong pens & I am extremely unhappy about it. I have not had a very good week with Amazon in particular.  I love Amazon, but I keep receiving packages that are damaged containing items that are damaged.  Now this mess arrives. Argh!  The pens are excellent in every regard. They just aren’t the colors ordered. I wanted the purple & yellow pens & as you can see they are not in my order.  I ordered a journal earlier this week that came with some pens & stencils & the pens are too thick to fit in the stencils. These do an amazing job in them. The stencils have very tight corners & are very sharp & these handle them beautifully. I just did not want to waste ink filling them in. Lol. The first thing I noticed about these pens was the heft. I love a pen with some heft to it. Even tho I’ve had hand surgery & I can no longer write, paint, or draw as long as I used to I have always loved the feel of a well balanced writing instrument in my hand. These aren’t exactly balanced lol bc of the ink distribution & the plastic fatigue finger rest, but it feels nice in my hand.  I’m just thoroughly ticked off that these are not what I paid for & what I have been waiting for. Lol.  Back to my pen search.

reviews.title: Arrived dinged up. Not happy.
reviews.text: It’s pretty, but it’s not very sturdy. Mine arrived looking like it had been dropped on its edges either before or during transit tho I suppose it could have happened in a warehouse somewhere.  Even if I was willing to overlook that- which I am most definitely not- I opened it up to see that the tabbed monthly pages were all bent and folded too.  They are just regular paper pages with a little tan at the top that has a protective tape over it to make it sturdier i guess. Clearly it does not make it stuffy enough to survive the shipping.  I briefly thought that I would keep it & try to make it work bc returns are such a hassle for me bc I am disabled.  I get really annoyed with having to watch out for porch pirates trying to steal my returns if I put them on my porch to wait for UPS.  I am both physically disabled & hearing impaired so I have 2 service dogs, but I have found that if I try to keep my returns inside my home until UPS arrives they either don’t ring my doorbell to alert my service dogs who then alert me or they leave before I can physically get myself to the door. So yeah- returns are a big deal to me. Lol.  Bc if miss the window for UPS to pick it up (they only try once now) I then have to take it to a drop off center. Did I mention I am disabled? Lol. And I don’t drive?  Yeah. Big time fun at my house with returns.  So then I would have to pay more for a taxi there & back than what the products are worth. Lol. Not to mention my pain & suffering throughout all of it.  I just can’t help feeling that sometimes stuff gets shipped that has already been dropped or dinged bc I have received an awful lot lately  & it’s really ticking me off.  If I wanted dropped & dinged stuff I would buy used not new!  Hence the very long winded diatribe of venting here.  Let’s see if Amazon will post it. Lol.

reviews.title: Pretty Flipping Awesome!
reviews.text: I’m a book freak & I adore mine!  I use fountain pens. Cheap ones off eBay I paid anywhere from 5 cents to 99 cents for up to my Montblanc pens & Pilot pens & they all work fine. Sure you may have a little paper on the end of ur nib once in a while, but to me it’s nbd bc it homemade paper & I think they did a marvelous job on it. I’m not generally a fan of the “antiquing” of anything. I usually hate it, but I fell in love w the silver paper in this journal & decided why not?  The only thing I would change is the closure. I hate the tab thingy. I prefer the wrap around string method to close my journals or anything that does not leave me any type of uneven surface to write on later.  It’s a neat design feature to some ppl & it does look good & cute, but it’s not my personal preference.  I would not let that keep me from buying another one though. Lol. I do hope they make them with a different closing option in the future though bc I love the size of the book & the superior craftsmanship.  It’s well worth the price!

reviews.title: First one mis-delivered to??? Replacement A+!
reviews.text: It’s beautiful. I wasn’t sure if I would be happy with it given the price I paid which I felt was costly, but I’m happy enough with it. Bought it to record bird sightings in my backyard. I’m disabled & I am trying to find new ways to keep my mind off chronic pain which can consume a lot of brain cells.  Sadly, I took a disastrous fall shortly after buying it bc my neighbor blamed my bird feeders for injuring a local squirrel that likes to raid my bird feeders even though I left food for the squirrels too. The exact same food. I kid you not, but the evil little bigger decided to get on a light branch I was advised to place the feeder on by a bird conservancy place that “should keep the squirrels off of it”. Ha!  The squirrel was limping from a fall. I went out & stood on a 36” crate & took a nasty fall & I now have to have another back surgery. Proof that no good deed goes unpunished as the saying goes. Lol.  The fall lead to a concussion & repeated blackouts & exacerbated sciatica & massive swelling on my head, face, butt, elbows, hips, knees, etc. lol. Literally everywhere that hit the ground when I fell. So the irony is I have not even been able to use my beautiful bird journal to record any bird sightings since I bought it bc I am laid up awaiting back surgery. The last one left me disabled 15 years ago. Anyone reading this please keep me (Sherri) & my family in ur prayers bc if my past surgery is anything to go by i & we will need it.  So… now that you know my life story & I have saved $500 on therapy… buy the journal bc it’s simply lovely. Lol.

reviews.title: I love it!
reviews.text: It’s pretty. The color is gorgeous. It has nice paper. I can use my fountain pens in it even the cheapest 99 cent ones I buy on eBay. Lol. What’s not to love?  But it bc you will not regret it. And truth bomb: I bought this for my grandson - and kept it! Lol. Yeah- I’m that b*tch!,  but I gave him something better in his opinion as a kid. Win-win!

reviews.title: Best purchase ever!!!!
reviews.text: Where has this been since I became disabled & mostly bedridden?  I’ve been through so many subpar bed trays it’s ridiculous. This one is a gem!  I absolutely love it!  I am stunned that my art easel actually fits it & even better two of the plastic legs nicely fit into the book ledge groove to keep it nice & steady while I draw & paint.  I love the ski sled legs because it makes it so easy to move when I have to get up. One of the previous types I tried was so heavy I could barely lift it due to my disabilities, but this is sturdy & light.  The only thing I might do is add 2 pieces of small rubber to the ski sled legs at the ends by my body for added stability so that it doesn’t move when I don’t want it to because I suffer with vertigo & sleep apnea & I don’t want it to move if I fall over. Lol. So I would still be able to just lightly lift the legs w the rubber attached & still be able to push it forward easily enough. The only other thing I miss & need is a cup holder as I am on medications & need to stay hydrated & do lots of arts & crafts where I need to have water handy. I understand they probably didn’t add it bc most ppl buy it to use as a laptop table & electronics & fluids are never a hood idea, but I wish I had the option to choose for myself. I’ve thought about drilling a hole in the top & adding a cup holder or more likely just adding one to the side. As I will likely add some cup holders for my pens, pencils, & brushes, & craft supplies. I also wish that they offered an even larger size.  For those of us who are stuck in our beds & literally live in them there are very few options that are not homemade.  I would love one to go the full length of my queen bed & have designed several of them. Lol. As I live alone with 2 service dogs there’s nobody to complain about me dropping beads in the bed or spiking paint on the sheets. Lol.  To the manufacturers: bravo on a well-designed product & please for the love of God & this disabled woman please make a larger option!!!!  Mine never leaves my bed. I just push it to the end of the bed & go to sleep & wake up the next morning & pull it back towards me & resume my crafting or bills or whatever I was doing the night before. Lol.  Oh- and sometime- yeah SOMETIMES- I even use it as a food tray. Imagine that!! Lol.

reviews.title: Hard as a rock!  Lumpy. Gross. Ugly!
reviews.text: I expected to love this journal Bc I love the color & I absolutely love glitter. However, what arrived is a hot mess. It’s hard as a rock on one entire side. There is no fluid & there is absolutely no consistency in this product. All of the glitter is bunched up & melted/solidified to one side of the journal. It’s vile. This was supposed to be a gift. Thank heaven I had it delivered to me for wrapping Bc I would have been absolutely mortified for the recipient to have received this & equated it’s total lack of quality with my feelings for the recipient.  I do not even understand how a product in this condition is being shipped by the manufacturer or Amazon. Shame on both of them. It’s been a complete waste of my time & my $ (spent looking for the item, waiting for the item, paying for the item & now having to return the item)!  Unreal this is offered for sale in this condition. Not cool ppl.

reviews.title: Obviously dropped while packing!
reviews.text: Aside from the fact that this was obviously dropped while being packed bc it has dirt on it & is so damaged I cannot believe it was even shipped I still cannot believe how lacking in quality these are.  I ordered two & while the second is in a little better shape I already know this will be a return for me. As a disabled person I tend to take falls & maybe the bad packaging person that dropped the book did me a favor by pointing out its obvious flaws.  The main reason I purchased these books to begin with was because the company donates a book for every book you buy and I always try to support companies that give back in this manner & to this degree, but for my personal needs these just won’t work. They just are not sturdy enough.  If they had arrived I damaged & I could have used them for a while & found that out for myself I probably would have given them a higher rating, but I think 3 stars is fair as they are usable for most oriole & priced okay currently. They are actually cheaper today than when I purchased them days ago.  Amazon always seems to lower prices after I purchase stuff. Lol. So much for Irish luck. Lol.  These will do for grocery lists or general to do lists, but you won’t want to trust your poetry or fine writing to these imo. The paper is very thin & see through & some of my pages are glued together weirdly. Idk why & it’s driving me crazy. Definitely a return.

reviews.title: Perfect!  Great size, refillable, & affordable! Trifecta!
reviews.text: Not the best pics, but I bought these to give to my kids & grandkids along with these pens I’m making for them with resin. I used temporary tattoos & then I sprayed a clear urethane over them so they the gold tattoos don’t run off & I make sure to place the tattoos above & below the rubber band thingy.  For less than $4 a kid my kids have a great planner that’s refillable & I can personalize each with animals they  like & I have since added their names using the creep $1 alphabet stickers you can buy most places.  I also do this with the black sketch books as you can see in one of the pics bc they can use them to sketch or for kites or to journal depending on the sketch book you buy. These are $3 black Daler Rowney drawing sketch books with Amazon bought temporary tattoos.  I sent my kids pics of the tattoos & let them pic their designs. The alphabet beads were also purchased on Amazon & I threaded them into the ink refills bc they kept trying to float up from the resin. I actually had to glue them to the refill bc the air spaces still made them want to float, but it was so much fun. It was my first foray into resin which didn’t go great die to some bad resin at first, but finally got some good stuff & had some fun.  I know I got off topic, but you can’t go wrong with these little journals imo.

reviews.title: Missing the lead in the pencil! Smells bad.
reviews.text: The pencils arrived with many broken tips which I sharpened, but one pencil does not even have a lead in it.  I kept sharpening it thinking maybe the lead broke off during manufacturing, but as you can see there’s no lead in there at all. It’s just an empty wooden shell!  If you have allergies or problems with strong smells prepare for an instant migraine which is what I had within 5 minutes of opening these pencils. It’s sad because they do seem to color okay, but between receiving a defective batch of pencils & the strong  & terrible odor I can’t endorse these for people with any types of allergies like mine. Amazon is supposed to send a replacement, but if they smell as bad as these do I’ll have to return them due to my allergies.  And seriously I’m an order with 3 items that arrived today 2 out of 3 arrived defective. This appears to be a manufacturing issue & the coloring book I ordered does as well unless the coloring book was damaged during packaging which was possible & utterly annoying too.  Idk what’s going on with the quality control ppl. I received resin molds last week that were also obviously damaged in the manufacturing process & still mailed out with globs of silicone left on the molds damaging them & making them unusable.  The quality control has gone way downhill at Amazon imo.

reviews.title: The Cadillac Case
reviews.text:
I was really excited to receive my new clipboard to replace my previous one which had started falling apart! My first thought on opening the box was "wow, this is huge". It's longer than my previous clipboard, so I wasn't sure how I would like toting it around at work (I'm an RN). However, the difference has been like trading up from a rickshaw to a Caddy. Not that there is anything wrong with a rickshaw!

My new clipboard fits everything but the kitchen sink (see attached pic). I wear my stethoscope, but can store it in the clipboard when I leave work, so I don't forget it at home and then have to wear one of those plastic yellow isolation-cart throwaway ones that don't work for poop. My pockets are usually BUSTING at the seams with all the stuff I like to carry around. No longer! I can cram it all inside this beast! I don't know how well it will hold up to my dropping it repeatedly, so I will post an update in a while with the durability factor.

P.S. I am one of those endlessly-researching people who look up reviews online for 7,456 items before deciding on one. You're welcome. I've done all the legwork for you. :-)

**Update, December 2016: This case is still perfect! No cracks, the top clip is still tightly secured, still feels really sturdy. :)

**Update, after dropping the case a few times over the years, a piece of the plastic broke. I'm buying a new one now. It lasted a really long time given the price!

reviews.title: BEST Pastel Pencil Sharpeners out there.
reviews.text: I use these for pastel pencils since they seem to be the only ones that actually sharpen and don't eat pencils down to half if you put into an electric sharpener. They go dull pretty quickly so its important to have extras on hand. I've tried about twelve different sharpeners including an electric one, which creates a very fine point for colored pencils but eats a third to even half the pencil. With these sharpeners, you're able to conserve some of your precious material so that it goes on paper and not the garbage. Win win!

reviews.title: A Colored Pencil, Charcoal Pencil and Graphite Pencil Artist's Best Friend.
reviews.text:
The point, oh the point. The point this bad boy gives your pencils turns them into literal spears...the lead point is so long! And the point gets SUPER sharp so you can get some of the FINEST DETAIL into your work. A fine point is actually the 'secret' of many artists today....the finer you can get the point, the more precise every square inch of your work will be. You want your tools working to the best of their advantage and this sharpener will make all your favorite tools do just that. It uses a USB to charge, which is convenient since I always have my computer nearby and can charge it up when I take food breaks.

NOTE: THIS WILL EAT CONTE PASTEL PENCILS AS THEY ARE TOO SOFT. The photos attached show Primo Charcoal Pencils and the difference of a regularly sharpened Berol Prismacolor pencil and one using this sharpener.

reviews.text: I have always been a little fearful of fertilizing my peace lilies, tip burn especially.  Most generic houseplant foods, no matter how weak I made the solution always burned the tips.  I took a chance on this fertilizer, being especially formulated for peace lilies, thought this might work.  I ordered, read the directions and used just half of the recommended dosage on all of my peace lilies.  All of them, I have 6, turned deeply green in just two weeks and all threw out new larger florets.  I am so pleased with this unique formula.  I have been using it every three to four weeks, still at half strength.  At this rate, I will have fertilizer for a long time. reviews.title: Dangerous bc metal not properly coated! Rough edges!
reviews.text: Where to begin?  I’ve been trying to get the 20 pics of these eyesores to upload since I received them, but they won’t. I ordered them bc one of my service dogs had emergency surgery & both pups were exposed to weed killer my LL put down, but I was unaware of & both pups became ill.  I knew when they arrived that I should have immediately returned them bc both boxes had the look about them that they were someone else’s previous returns.  The bad tape jobs on the boxes are generally a pretty good indicator imo. Both kennels had been placed together in one larger box for shipping so they should neither of them have had such a horrific tape job applied to them. I’ve purchased Midwest kennels for over 35 years & I’ve never purchased them with this kind of tape job in my life.  These were not “factory sealed”.  These hasd obviously been opened & returned. Worse- it looked as tho someone kept the new kennel & returned their old one bc you can literally see where all the powder coating is missing on these kennels which happens over time from use & friction.  One piece in particular has no coating on it whatsoever as can be seen in the photos that won’t load. Lol.  I thought I was buying direct from the manufacturer this time as I’ve moved away from buying from third party sellers due to receiving items like these kennels.  What’s annoying is I desperately needed this for a dog post surgery & im left with an un-safe kennel.  The metal is jagged throughout. I’ve cut my own hands numerous times bc the costing is missing & the metal is bare & rough.  Either the quality of Midwest has taken a nosedive in the 4 yrs since I last purchased a kennel or someone sent me used items.  I cannot recommend this item bc it is dangerous to ur pups eyes, nose, skin, paws, fur, etc.  jagged edges have no business near animal nor human bodies.
